correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the displayed SRK-I and SRK-II stage equations against Ye 2026 §2.2, and independently substituted the affine gradient K(x-m). Both give exactly e_{k+1}=(I-hK+h²K²/2)e_k+sqrt(2)(Delta B_k-K J_k) pathwise for any real symmetric quadratic K and shared Brownian pairs. The Gaussian covariance of (Delta B,J) is [[h,h²/2],[h²/2,h³/3]]⊗I, giving Q=2h(I-hK+h²K²/3), strictly positive in every eigendirection. For SPD K, r(z)=1-z+z²/2∈(0,1) iff 0<z<2, so a unique invariant law exists iff 0<h lambda_max(K)<2; if an r>=1 eigenmode exists, the positive Gaussian noise yields no invariant probability by the characteristic-function iteration. Scalar Lyapunov balance gives Sigma_h=K^{-1}f(hK), f=(1-z+z²/3)/(1-z+z²/2-z³/8). Its exact defect is z²(3z-4)/(24(1-z+z²/2-z³/8)), with denominator positive on 0<z<2 and sole positive zero 4/3. For all eigenmodes to match K^{-1} requires K=lambda I, h=4/(3lambda). At this step r=5/9 and stationary covariance 1/lambda, giving lim_(N→∞)(Nh) Var(N^-1 Σ Z_k)=14/(3lambda²) versus 2/lambda² for the continuous-time OU integral, ratio 7/3. Independently constructed a separate SymPy stage/noise/variance identity script (not copied from verify.py) and checked all these polynomial identities, Brownian covariance multiplication, stability boundary and long-run ratio exactly; independently reconstructed the seven-blob Git tree SHA-1 557c09b938395d675525e9e6dab13e776d74369b. Finite stage examples are corroboration, while universal claims follow from the algebra and spectral decomposition.

value.rationale: The two stochastic Runge–Kutta samplers are concrete modern algorithms with distinct gradient-stage budgets. Their exact coincidence on Gaussian targets is a useful caution for benchmarking; the sharp nonzero stationarity resonance and anisotropic obstruction separate target marginal accuracy from step-size stability. At the sole isotropic exactness step the physical-time average variance is 7/3 of the continuous OU coefficient, a nontrivial quantitative demonstration that an exact invariant marginal need not make time averages efficient. Even comparing against the exact OU sampled on the same mesh gives a strictly larger penalty (numerically 4.6667 vs 2.2879 in units lambda^-2). The theorem is a motivated exact benchmark, not only a textbook AR identity or an arbitrary numerical slice; its limitation to quadratic fixed-step algorithms and unequal-work comparison is explicit.

limitations: Pathwise identity requires exact coupling of both Brownian functionals. Stationary Gaussian results require SPD K, stable h and the exact source scheme coefficients; neither applies to nonquadratic U.

The 7/3 comparison is between stationarily initialized discrete mesh-time averages and continuously observed diffusion averages at equal physical time; not equal computational cost or equal sampling mesh.
The independent symbolic verification of formulas is not Lean or expert attestation, and finite checks do not prove an infinite-domain theorem independently of algebra.
Originality is best-of-knowledge with unindexed test-equation priority risk; 2023 harmonic BAOA article full text was not inspected.
